chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Jamīl, from some of our companions, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, that he said:
“The thief is not to have his hand cut off until he confesses to the theft twice. Then if he retracts, he is liable for the stolen property, and his hand is not cut off when there are no witnesses.”

key_terms.السَّارِقُ: the thief, the person accused or proven to have committed theft
key_terms.السَّرِقَةِ: the act of theft or the stolen property in context
key_terms.شُهُودٌ: witnesses whose testimony establishes the matter
key_terms.ضَمِنَ: he becomes liable to compensate or restore
key_terms.مَرَّتَيْنِ: twice, indicating the required repetition of confession
key_terms.يُقِرَّ: to confess or admit legally before authority

ai.seo_question: When is the hadd punishment for theft established according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding the hadd punishment for theft. It indicates that the punishment is not carried out merely on a single confession, and that if the confession is withdrawn and there are no witnesses, financial liability remains but the corporal hadd is not enforced.
